title: Cyrus and the Drop
premise: Bram Amberdale, an analyst fired from three intelligence agencies for trusting his gut over the data, receives a call on a burner phone he never bought — and hears his own voice on the other end. The caller is a deepfake built from his old case files, deployed by a rogue cell inside a private security consortium to frame him for a staged infrastructure collapse in the port city of Grayhaven. To clear his name, Bram must infiltrate the consortium's shell network with help from three fellow castoffs: a disgraced forensic accountant, a fired signal technician, and a young courier who has no file at all. As they unravel the plot — a gas main breach timed to look like municipal negligence — Bram realizes the voice on the phone is being puppeteered by his former mentor, who chose him as the fall guy precisely because no one would believe him. In the climax Bram exposes the attack minutes before detonation, forcing the mentor to choose between the operation and the last shred of the man he used to be; the mentor's hesitation lets Bram trigger the shutdown, though the mentor dies covering their escape. The book ends with Bram still unemployable but no longer alone, keeping the go-bag unpacked for the first time in years.
about_author: Dominic Thornbury is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing 'accidents' that were anything but. He writes thrillers about people the system files under 'unreliable' and then forgets.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A quiet Tuesday in his rented room above a laundromat: we see the go-bag by the door, the rehearsed cover story, the rejection letters pinned like trophies of failure. He gets a polite final notice from a fourth agency. The beat is weary routine — a man who has made exile comfortable.

chapters.title: Wrong Number
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A burner phone taped under his own mailbox rings. On the line: his own voice, reading coordinates in Grayhaven's dock district. He traces nothing, finds no sender, and tells himself it's a prank until the voice says something only Bram knows — the real reason he was fired from his first job.

chapters.title: Three Names on a Wall
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, flashback braided in. He maps his three firings on paper and finds a pattern: each dismissal followed a report he filed about Halcyon Meridian Group, a private security consortium. The emotional beat is vindication curdling into dread — someone has been following his career like a case study.

chapters.title: Grayhaven
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He takes a bus to the port city and walks the coordinates: a decommissioned pumping station slated for demolition, fenced, guarded by contractors wearing Halcyon badges. He photographs everything and is spotted. The beat is the hunter realizing he is also the bait.

chapters.title: The Courier With No File
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A nineteen-year-old document courier notices she's been handed two identical delivery slips with different timestamps — a classic alibi build. Instinct honed on the streets makes her keep one copy instead of delivering it. The beat is small defiance that will matter enormously later.

chapters.title: Frame Job
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. His face appears on news feeds as a person of interest in an 'imminent threat assessment' leak — planted evidence, dated tomorrow. He realizes the burner call wasn't a warning to him; it was a rehearsal, testing whether his voiceprint could pass. Panic becomes clarity: he has days.

chapters.title: An Accountant Who Counts Wrong
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Disgraced forensic accountant Odile Vasseur spots a $40,000 anomaly in Grayhaven utility filings — insurance premiums tripled on a building scheduled to burn. She posts her finding on a dead forum Bram haunts. The beat is two paranoiacs recognizing each other's handwriting.

chapters.title: Found Family, First Draft
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He meets Odile in a 24-hour diner; mutual vetting via shared enemies. She brings Wren, who brings the duplicate slip. Three people with nothing left decide to pool what remains. The beat is cautious trust — the first warm thing any of them has touched in years.

chapters.title: Signal Lost
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Fired signal technician Teodor Brandt, living out of his van, intercepts odd burst transmissions near the pumping station on a hobbyist rig. He doesn't know what they mean, but he knows the encryption suite — it's government-surplus, sold off to Halcyon. The beat is professional longing: finally, a puzzle worth solving.

chapters.title: Four Chairs
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Teodor joins the group after Bram buys him breakfast and admits he needs help, which costs him visibly. They map the plot: a gas main breach at the station during a city inspection tour, blamed on neglected infrastructure — and on the whistleblower who flagged it. Bram. The beat is resolve hardening into a plan.

chapters.title: The Voice Again
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The burner calls again; this time Bram talks back. The fake-Bram taunts him with details of his firings, then slips — uses a phrase his old mentor Marcus Ilves always used. Bram goes cold. The beat is grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: What Marcus Taught Me
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, long flashback chapter. His apprenticeship under Ilves: the man who taught him to read patterns, who defended him once, whose own career died in the same purge that took Halcyon's rivals. The beat is love and betrayal occupying the same memory, neither winning.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the money through four shells, Odile finds the payout structure: the attack is insured, the insurer is owned by Halcyon, and the beneficiary signature is a dead man's — Marcus Ilves, officially deceased two years. The beat is triumph shadowed by confusion: why would a ghost need money?

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Bram and Wren's POV alternating. Using Wren's courier access, they get inside the Halcyon field office. Bram copies a drive; Wren covers by being exactly the invisible girl everyone overlooks. They nearly get caught when Bram hesitates at a photo of Ilves on the wall. The beat is fear metabolized into competence.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Decryption marathon in the van. The drive contains the attack timeline — 72 hours — plus something stranger: psychological profiles of each of the four of them, compiled over months. They weren't discovered; they were selected. The beat is violation, and the terrible intimacy of being studied.

chapters.title: Chosen
chapters.summary: Group scene, Bram's POV dominant. Why these four? Because each was discarded by institutions, each has motive to hate Halcyon, and each is plausible as a lone conspirator. The plan needs scapegoats in depth. Wren breaks down; Odile steadies her. The beat is the found family choosing itself harder because someone tried to weaponize its formation.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram reaches Marcus directly through the burner: 'I know you're alive.' A meeting is set — neutral ground, thirty minutes. Bram tells the others, against operational sense, because he refuses to lie to them. The beat is loyalty tested by the oldest loyalty of all.

chapters.title: Two Men and a Table
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Marcus, alive and hollowed out, explains: faking his death freed him to run the operation as Halcyon's deniable asset; framing Bram was sentiment — he wanted to give his best student a role in history. Bram offers him a way out: stop the clock, testify, be a ghost no longer. Marcus wavers. The beat is a mentorship ending in a held breath.

chapters.title: Clock Runs
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. The meeting was traced; Halcyon moves the attack up twelve hours and burns the safe house. The four scatter and regroup at the pumping station perimeter with improvised tools: Odile's financial kill-switch on the insurance, Teodor's jammer, Wren's knowledge of the maintenance tunnels. The beat is no-plan momentum — courage without comfort.

chapters.title: Pumping Station
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, high-tempo. Inside the station, Bram reaches the detonation controller as the inspection convoy approaches. Teodor jams the trigger link; Odile freezes the payout remotely; Wren guides evacuation of the tour party away from the blast radius. Marcus arrives, gun drawn, ordered to finish it. The beat is every thread pulled taut at once.

chapters.title: The Hesitation
chapters.summary: Bram and Marcus's POV interwoven. Ordered to shoot, Marcus looks at Bram and sees the analyst he built, not the traitor he scripted. His two-second pause lets Bram trigger the manual shutdown. Halcyon's cleanup team fires; Marcus turns and returns it, buying the others the exit, and falls. The beat is sacrifice as the only honest sentence left to him.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Bram's POV weeks later. Halcyon's shells are bleeding out through Odile's leaked ledgers; the four are officially nobodies again, which suits them. Bram mails his testimony to a journalist anyway — truth over safety, a lesson learned late. Final image: the go-bag open on the bed, empty, staying empty. The beat is belonging, chosen and kept.
